title: SSE chunk coalescer and atomic-call lease for reconnect-safe function calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a server-side chunk coalescer and an atomic-call lease token to reduce reconnect overhead and ensure idempotent function/tool call semantics over SSE streams. Aim is to improve application-level correctness and reduce duplicate tool invocations under flaky client networks without requiring clients to adopt a new wire protocol.
technical_notes: Background: current SSE implementation emits many micro-chunks for every token (token-per-event) which causes clients that reconnect frequently to replay many small events and can trigger duplicate function/tool calls. Proposal: 1) Coalesce short adjacent events on the server into a bounded-size composite chunk (meta-event) with a lightweight header that preserves original per-token ordering metadata; 2) Attach a short-lived atomic-call lease token to events containing function/tool call intents so the server and downstream agents can negotiate ownership and safe replay; 3) Maintain backward compatibility by encoding the coalesced envelope as a superset of existing JSONL events so EventSource clients continue to parse incrementally if they choose. Implementation involves changes in the serving runtime's SSE writer, the output-serialization layer, and the reconnect handling in the HTTP gateway.
acceptance_criteria: SSE writer can emit coalesced composite-chunk events (<= 32KB) that contain multiple logical fragments with per-fragment sequence numbers and checksums.
When a reconnect occurs, clients using the existing EventSource path can resume from the last acknowledged fragment sequence and not re-execute function calls if server-side lease is still active.
Atomic-call lease tokens expire after configurable TTL and are audited in logs with lease-granted and lease-revoked events.
No change in API surface for basic streaming clients; coalesced events are backwards-compatible and incremental parseable by our SDKs.
End-to-end integration test demonstrates: simulated flaky network -> reconnect -> no duplicate external tool invocations in 1000 trial runs.
Performance: median first-byte latency increase < 2ms when coalescing enabled; token throughput preserved within 5% of baseline under typical workloads.
tasks: Design composite-chunk envelope (header fields: stream_id, frag_seq, frag_count, frag_checksum, lease_token_opt)
Implement coalescer in streaming runtime (config flag: sse.coalescer.enabled, max_chunk_bytes)
Emit lease tokens for events with function/tool-call intents and persist lease state in ephemeral store (ttl configurable)
Gateway reconnect handler: accept resume request with last_frag_seq and optional lease token assertion
Client SDKs: add optional resume helpers and parse helpers for composite chunks (non-breaking)
Add e2e test harness (chaos netem) and unit tests for parity/checksum validation and lease expiry
Add console metrics: coalesced_chunks/sec, average_fragments_per_chunk, lease_grants/sec, lease_conflicts
risks: If coalescer buffer sizing is wrong, we may increase tail latency for some short-lived requests
Lease tokens introduce a transient stateful component; mismanagement could cause missed tool invocations (false negatives)
Older proxies or streaming middleboxes may split composite events in unexpected places; must verify heuristics and add validation backstops
tradeoffs: We prioritize correctness of function/tool calls over minimal added complexity. The coalescer trades a small potential increase in output aggregation latency for fewer reconnect roundtrips and less duplicated downstream work. Alternative was to move lease logic entirely to clients (requires client changes and rollout dependency); we avoid that to preserve PLG experience.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: spec and wire-format (this ticket) + unit tests. Phase 2: runtime coalescer + gateway resume support behind feature flag. Phase 3: rollout to canary, enable lease tokens for tool-call-heavy routes, monitor metrics and anomaly alerts. Phase 4: SDK helpers and docs. Rollback path: disable sse.coalescer.enabled and revoke leases.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope encode/decode, checksum validation, lease expiry. Integration tests: simulate reconnect patterns (immediate reconnect, delayed reconnect > lease TTL) and assert no duplicate tool invocations. Load test with 10k concurrent SSE clients to measure throughput and latency. Add chaos tests that fragment TCP packets and ensure EventSource clients can reassemble.
notes:
- Keep the composite envelope as a JSON top-level object so existing JSONL-based client parsers can incrementally parse when fragments are full JSON objects.
- Lease tokens are short (default 10s) and renewed on active client heartbeats. For long-lived tool calls (external webhooks) we fall back to persistent idempotency keys (server-side).
